examples.explanation: The two 'o's would need to become different letters ('a' and 'r').
The renaming p->t, a->i, e->l, r->e is consistent in both directions.

hints: Walk both strings in lockstep, remembering the last position where each character was seen.
Characters match exactly when their previous occurrence indices agree on both sides.
One-directional mapping is not enough: 'ab' vs 'aa' must fail, so check both directions (or last-seen positions).
title: 331. Isomorphic Strings
